Edition match: The photographed Ravensburger box includes the English subtitle 'Depart for the adventure of a life time' alongside French and Dutch. The Ravensburger English rulebook cited by this record identifies Wolfgang Kramer, Michael Kiesling and the same Australia release.. Original image URL: https://images.tcdn.com.br/img/img_prod/558884/australia_888903184_1_ad786d2c5e7556f71d7039927058ed1f.jpg. firstPlayerRule: The player who thinks they know the most about Australia goes first, or the group may choose a starter by any method.
clarifications: The youngest player takes the first setup card, with setup picks continuing around the table; this does not determine who takes the first game turn.
The simple and full games use the same opening rule. Turns proceed clockwise.

internalEvidence: Read the eight-page English Ravensburger booklet through the indexed PDF. Its cover identifies Ravensburger game no. 26358-5. PDF page 3 gives the youngest player first setup-card selection; page 4 gives the Australia-knowledge criterion, open choice and clockwise turns. Page 7 states that the full game uses the simple-game rules except for listed additions. Rangers, aeroplanes and conservation/industrialization tiles match inventory BGG 15033. The source host denied a direct file download, so no file hash is asserted. Owner authorized assistant review on 2026-09-22. Editorial review 2026-09-24: Rechecked the opening instruction, game identity and named edition against the rulebook. Label edit 2026-09-25: removed file/print bookkeeping from the edition label; rule content unchanged.
uncertainty: Knowledge of Australia is self-assessed; the rules prescribe no comparison or tie procedure. The alternative is intentionally open-ended.
